title: [DocDb] Wait queues unfair for multi-tablet transactions
body:
Jira Link: [DB-8837](https://<redacted-host>/browse/DB-8837)
### Description

`TestMultiTabletFairnessOfWaitQueues` automation is failing due to unfair wait queue on `2.20.0.0-b75`

Test steps:
```
1. Create universe with wait_queues and read committed isolation level enabled
2. Create DB and a range sharded table
3. Insert values across all ranges
4. Execute following steps for each isolation level:
5. start 100 threads:
    begin transaction
    select;
    acquire for update lock on 1 common row + n random rows (each from different tablet)
    store transaction number that has acquired lock in global list
    wait for all transactions to start
    commit
6. Validate that global list contains all transaction numbers in sequential order
```

The test is failing at step 6 for repeatable read & serializable isolation level and passing for read committed.

### Issue Type

kind/bug

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: I updated the testcase to run only 3 threads sequentially attempting to acquire locks on batch of rows belonging to different tablets. This whole scenario is run 100 times in a loop as suggested by @participant2 but I am still running into unfair wait_queues.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
The result from test failure:
```
(   806.521s) Run 3 transactions sequentially in read committed isolation level : >>> Integration Test Failed <<< 
Transactions didn't acquire lock in expected order for read committed isolation level
Expected:[1, 2, 3]
Got:[1, 3, 2]
```
The above failed in 59th cycle of running the 3 transactions.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: The test case is blocked on this issue. @participant2 did you get a chance to investigate this further?

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
One failure mode here seems to be the following:
1. Txn 1 locks k1 and k2
2. Txn 2 attempts to lock k1, gets blocked
3. Txn 3 attempts to lock k2, gets blocked
4. Txn 1 commits
5. Txn 3 is unblocked on k2, successfully writes lock
6. Txn 2 is unblocked on k1, successfully writes lock, and only then will attempt request to k2, getting blocked behind Txn 3

Txn 2 is issuing a statement like `SELECT * FROM table WHERE k in (k1, k2, .......);`, which results in multiple requests to different tablets (k1 and k2 are at different tablets), but if the request for k1 is blocked, then the request for k2 is not sent until the k1 request returns
